info.comment: Begin info at its lowercase bounded header through following directives. info.md#detection: Entry 12 of [detection.md](../detection.md) selects the exact lower-case prefix `info`, without a suffix boundary. info.md#keyword-boundaries: Both fixed keywords are case-sensitive and require immediate common whitespace, `%%` or end of text. common.md#leading-whitespace: Whitespace, line terminators, directives, and comment regions before the first unit of the diagram's lexer are trivia and are not seen by the diagram's grammar. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

patterns.comment: Reuse hidden YAML and its shared line-based approximation. info.md#hidden-yaml: At a unit start, `---`, zero or more ASCII spaces/tabs and LF open hidden YAML, even off a physical line start.

Reuse the native hidden directive form. info.md#hidden-directive-and-line-endings: After optional ASCII padding, hidden DIRECTIVE reads `%%{` and arbitrary content through the earliest `}%%` followed by LF, common whitespace or EOF.
Reuse native percent comments. info.md#comments-and-common-trivia: The native comment rule reads optional ASCII indentation, `%%` and maximal text before physical EOL.

Read the bounded showInfo flag through following directives. info.md#keyword-boundaries: Both fixed keywords are case-sensitive and require immediate common whitespace, `%%` or end of text. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.
patterns.name: keyword.control.mermaid

patterns.comment: Reuse the common title and accessibility forms. info.md#composite-common-forms: At any unit start optional ASCII indentation may precede a common form. `title-line` reads `title` alone, or `title`, one ASCII space/tab and possibly empty line text. `acc-title-line` reads `accTitle`, zero or more ASCII spaces/tabs, a colon and possibly empty line text; `acc-descr-line` does so with `accDescr`. info.md#composite-common-forms: The block alternative reads `accDescr`, zero or more common whitespace characters, `{` and arbitrary content through the first `}`.
